title: Distributed filesystems, HDFS and object storage as a data lake

videos.script: Every job so far has read a file from one disk. On a real cluster, there is no one disk. {{disks}} Each worker is a different computer, and a path on one of them means nothing on the others. So a cluster needs a filesystem that every machine sees the same way. {{shared}} This lesson builds one. HDFS, with a namenode that remembers where everything is, and four datanodes that hold the bytes. {{hdfs}} You will put a year of clicks into it, and watch it become ten blocks, each stored three times. {{blocks}} Then you will kill a datanode, and watch the copies come back on their own. {{repair}} Last, the other way to store a lake: an object store, the kind every cloud sells. It has no directories and no rename, and that one missing operation explains more of this course than you would expect. {{objects}}
